name: MI-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a +15 Republican PVI
Moolenaar is a well-funded incumbent with $1.9M on hand
Challenger Ambrose raised only $85K with minimal cash
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Moolenaar: a +15 Republican district, incumbency, and a roughly 20-to-1 fundraising advantage over Ambrose. Markets price the race at 98% Republican, and no polls or expert ratings suggest movement, so the forecast stays near the baseline.
model.watch: A major outside-spending surge or an unexpected scandal involving Moolenaar would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Michigan's 2nd District is solidly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of about 15 points toward the GOP. Republican incumbent John Moolenaar is running for reelection with a large financial edge, holding roughly $1.9 million after raising over $1.6 million. Democratic challenger Ben Ambrose has raised about $85,000 and has limited cash on hand, with no outside spending reported on either side. A Green Party and an independent candidate are also on the ballot but show no measurable support. Prediction markets give Moolenaar about a 98% chance of winning, and no polls or expert ratings indicate a competitive race. Absent unforeseen developments, Moolenaar is strongly favored to return to Congress.
